The value can be either JSON or Airflow's URI format. .. _connection-serialization-json-example: JSON format example ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ .. versionadded:: 2.3.0 If serializing with JSON: .. code-block:: bash export AIRFLOW_CONN_MY_PROD_DATABASE='{ "conn_type": "my-conn-type", "login": "my-login", "password": "my-password", "host": "my-host", "port": 1234, "schema": "my-schema", "extra": { "param1": "val1", "param2": "val2" } }' Generating a JSON connection representation """"""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""""" .. versionadded:: 2.8.0 To make connection JSON generation easier, the :py:class:`~airflow.models.connection.Connection` class has a convenience property :py:meth:`~airflow.models.connection.Connection.as_json`. It can be used like so: .. code-block:: pycon >>> from airflow.sdk import Connection >>> c = Connection( ... conn_id="some_conn", ... conn_type="mysql", ... description="connection description", ... host="myhost.com", ... login="myname", ... password="mypassword", ... extra={"this_param": "some val", "that_param": "other val*"}, ... ) >>> print(f"AIRFLOW_CONN_{c.conn_id.upper()}='{c.as_json()}'") AIRFLOW_CONN_SOME_CONN='{"conn_type": "mysql", "description": "connection description", "host": "myhost.com", "login": "myname", "password": "mypassword", "extra": {"this_param": "some val", "that_param": "other val*"}}' In addition, same approach could be used

the CLI.
